newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Apr Hub natgas ends lower after slow session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Apr Hub natgas ends lower after slow session.

text.p: NYMEX April Henry Hub natgas futures finished lower Wednesday in another range-bound, quiet session, as milder weather forecasts tempered physical demand and April failed to retest support, industry sources said.
April ended 0.1 cent lower at $1.896 per mmBtu after reaching a low of $1.865 early in the session. May settled up 1.1 cents at $1.946, while other deferreds were on either side of unchanged.
In ACCESS, April fell 1.6 cents to $1.88 following the release of American Gas Association storage data, showing a decline of 45 bcf to 886 bcf, or 218 bcf ahead of year-ago.
In the East, stocks were down 57 bcf to 469 bcf, while producing region inventories gained 14 bcf to 254 bcf. In the West, stocks edged two bcf lower to 163 bcf.
Technical support in April was seen at $1.85, and then at the March 3 low of $1.78 and the $1.701 contract low. Resistance was at $1.915, and then at $1.94-1.95, $2 and the mid-teens, traders said.
Ahead of April's expiry on Monday, traders are pegging May support at $1.90 and $1.845 and resistance at $1.99 and $2.04.

NYMEX's 12-month strip rose 1.3 cents today to $2.072, as an estimated 25,669 Hub contracts traded. Open interest for March 18 slipped 145 lots to 181,242 after hitting a record-high of 181,387 on Monday.
April Hub gas options expire this Friday.

The swing cash market continued to mirror futures, as Gulf Coast prices drifted three cents lower to the mid-to-high $1.80s. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes were similarly lower in the mid-$1.70s, with Chicago quoted at $1.95-1.97. At the New York city-gate, prices fell at least five cents to the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s, while Appalachian values were off a similar amount to about $2.
Weather Services Corp is calling for milder temperatures in the Northeast and Midwest by Thursday or Friday, with highs as much as 20 degrees above normal expected in the upper Midwest.
For next week, temperatures across most of the U.S. are expected to be seasonable, except in the Southwest where the heat is expected to remain.
Separately, no Permian or Alberta gas futures traded.
On the KCBT, April finished unchanged at $1.70 but even with current cash values. Deferreds were flat to one cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.6 cent to 19.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
Despite well above-normal temperatures in the Southwest, Permian basin cash prices were talked about five cents lower in the high-$1.60s.
